summary: Priority fanout starvation triggering 5xx and runtime GPU pin during tenant burst
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-12 14:30 UTC we observed a sustained elevation in 5xx errors (502/503) for BrightWrite's tenant on prod-us-east. Error rate rose from baseline ~0.2% to ~9% during a 30-minute burst and correlated with a sharp increase in streaming session resets and API gateway connection drops. Impact: customer reports timeouts in real-time chat sessions and degraded SLAs for critical routes. Environment: Dedicated pool (dedicated-nyc-1), prod-us-east, affected models pinned to open_llama_70b and redwood-optimized-13b. Steps to reproduce: 1) Simulate tenant burst using priority-tagged streaming requests (sustained concurrency ramp to tenant limit). 2) Observe apigw accept-queue growth and runtime worker preemption. 3) Note long-running keystore lock operations during ephemeral certificate refresh. Observed behavior: accept queue growth -> api-gateway hedged retry amplification -> serving-runtime reports blocked worker threads and elevated GPU utilization on a subset of pods (sustained high utilization on GPU 0 with curator process pinned). Keystore operations show repeated short stall spikes (~50-200ms) during curl-based ticket refreshes which appear to coincide with bursts. Logs: sample apigw traces show repeated upstream resets with "upstream prematurely closed connection" and runtime logs contain repeated "worker stalled waiting on keystore lock" and "gpu-eviction: pinned context". Metrics: apigw request duration P95 jumped to 1.8s, 5xx rate peaked at 9%, runtime watchdog evictions increased by 3x. Customer impact: chat sessions failing mid-stream; BrightWrite observes user-visible errors and elevated support tickets. Temporary mitigation applied: ingress rate-cap for tenant and scheduled keystore refresh stagger introduced. Investigation continues.
steps_to_reproduce: From a staging load generator, tag requests with tenant-priority header and ramp concurrent streaming sessions to tenant limit.
Monitor apigw accept-queue, runtime worker thread states, and GPU utilization across pods.
Trigger keystore refresh (rotate ephemeral cert) while burst is active to surface contention.
Observe 502/503 spike and streaming resets in traces.

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: priority-based fanout caused accept-queue skew; overloaded apigw threads retried requests increasing load on runtimes.
Keystore refreshes coinciding with bursts produced short global locks that serialised parts of the runtime request path, amplifying latency.
GPU pinning appears confined to a small set of runtime pods (runtime-7b6f, runtime-4c2a) where per-process contexts were not reclaimed promptly after preemption.
Reproduced locally in a scaled-down repro by combining sustained prioritized streaming with forced keystore rotation; reproduced 5xx and worker stalls.
Observed interaction between scheduler preemption policy and runtime GC that delays context switch leading to temporary pinned GPU contexts under heavy thread-blocking.

next_steps: Merge runtime PR that converts keystore critical section to read-write lock and cut a hotfix release (PR referenced).
Add safer keystore refresh stagger to default config for dedicated pools and ensure rollout via config management.
Tune scheduler preemption window to avoid prolonged GPU context pinning during heavy streaming bursts.
Follow up with BrightWrite postmortem and offer credits for SLA misses if verified.
resolution: Workaround: applied tenant ingress rate cap and staggered keystore refreshes which reduced 5xx rate to acceptable levels. Patch queued to convert keystore lock and a scheduler preemption tune will be released in hotfix. Customer notified and monitoring for 48 hours.
